questions.q: What are the products of aerobic respiration?
questions.qAf: Wat is die produkte van aërobiese respirasie?
questions.explain: Glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy (ATP). It is the reverse of photosynthesis.
questions.explainAf: Glukose + suurstof → koolstofdioksied + water + energie (ATP). Dit is die omgekeerde van fotosintese.

questions.q: Bread dough rises when yeast is added. What makes it rise?
questions.qAf: Brooddeeg rys wanneer gis bygevoeg word. Wat laat dit rys?
options: Carbon dioxide made by the yeast fermenting sugar
Lactic acid made by the yeast
optionsAf: Koolstofdioksied wat die gis maak wanneer dit suiker fermenteer
questions.explain: Yeast is a fungus. It ferments sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide, and the gas bubbles make the dough rise.
questions.explainAf: Gis is 'n swam. Dit fermenteer suiker tot etanol en koolstofdioksied, en die gasborrels laat die deeg rys.

questions.q: Why does aerobic respiration release far more energy than anaerobic respiration?
questions.qAf: Waarom stel aërobiese respirasie baie meer energie vry as anaërobiese respirasie?
options: It uses oxygen to break glucose down completely (36–38 ATP compared with 2)
optionsAf: Dit gebruik suurstof om glukose heeltemal af te breek (36–38 ATP teenoor 2)
Dit vind net in plante plaas
Dit vind net in die nag plaas
questions.explain: Aerobic respiration in the mitochondria makes 36–38 ATP per glucose. Anaerobic respiration in the cytoplasm makes only 2.
questions.explainAf: Aërobiese respirasie in die mitochondria maak 36–38 ATP per glukose. Anaërobiese respirasie in die sitoplasma maak net 2.

questions.q: Nitrogen makes up 78% of the air, but most plants cannot use it directly. How do plants get the nitrogen they need?
questions.qAf: Stikstof maak 78% van die lug uit, maar die meeste plante kan dit nie direk gebruik nie. Hoe kry plante die stikstof wat hulle nodig het?
options: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the soil turn it into nitrates that plants absorb
Leaves absorb it from the air during photosynthesis
Animals breathe it out for the plants
optionsAf: Stikstofbindende bakterieë in die grond verander dit in nitrate wat plante opneem
Blare neem dit tydens fotosintese uit die lug op
Diere asem dit vir die plante uit
questions.explain: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria, in the soil and in the root nodules of legumes, convert N₂ into nitrates (NO₃⁻).
questions.explainAf: Stikstofbindende bakterieë, in die grond en in die wortelknoppies van peulplante, omskep N₂ in nitrate (NO₃⁻).

questions.q: How does tuberculosis (TB) usually spread from person to person?
questions.qAf: Hoe versprei tuberkulose (TB) gewoonlik van persoon tot persoon?
options: Through air droplets from coughing and sneezing
optionsAf: Deur lugdruppels van hoes en nies
questions.explain: TB is caused by bacteria (Mycobacterium) and spreads through air droplets. Malaria is spread by mosquitoes and cholera by contaminated water.
questions.explainAf: TB word deur bakterieë (Mycobacterium) veroorsaak en versprei deur lugdruppels. Malaria word deur muskiete versprei en cholera deur besmette water.

questions.q: What does the atomic number of an element tell you?
questions.qAf: Wat sê die atoomgetal van 'n element vir jou?
options: The number of protons in its nucleus
optionsAf: Die aantal protone in sy kern
questions.explain: Atomic number = number of protons (= number of electrons in a neutral atom). Protons plus neutrons is the mass number.
questions.explainAf: Atoomgetal = aantal protone (= aantal elektrone in 'n neutrale atoom). Protone plus neutrone is die massagetal.

questions.q: Chlorine has an atomic number of 17 and a mass number of 35. How many neutrons does one chlorine atom have?
questions.qAf: Chloor het 'n atoomgetal van 17 en 'n massagetal van 35. Hoeveel neutrone het een chlooratoom?
questions.explain: Neutrons = 35 − 17 = 18.
questions.explainAf: Neutrone = 35 − 17 = 18.

questions.q: How did Henry Moseley improve the periodic table in 1913?
questions.qAf: Hoe het Henry Moseley die periodieke tabel in 1913 verbeter?
options: He ordered the elements by atomic number instead of atomic mass
He noticed that every eighth element was similar
optionsAf: Hy het die elemente volgens atoomgetal in plaas van atoommassa gerangskik
Hy het opgemerk dat elke agtste element soortgelyk is
questions.explain: Moseley used X-rays to show that elements should be ordered by atomic number (protons). Newlands noticed the octaves.
questions.explainAf: Moseley het X-strale gebruik om te wys dat elemente volgens atoomgetal (protone) gerangskik moet word. Newlands het die oktawe opgemerk.

questions.q: What happens to the size of atoms as you go down a group of the periodic table?
questions.qAf: Wat gebeur met die grootte van atome soos jy in 'n groep van die periodieke tabel afgaan?
options: They get bigger, because there are more electron shells
They get smaller, because there are more protons
optionsAf: Hulle word groter, omdat daar meer elektrondoppe is
Hulle word kleiner, omdat daar meer protone is
questions.explain: Atomic radius increases down a group (more shells) and decreases across a period from left to right.
questions.explainAf: Atoomradius neem toe in 'n groep af (meer doppe) en neem af oor 'n periode van links na regs.

questions.q: Why does a bicycle tyre get harder as you pump more air into it?
questions.qAf: Waarom word 'n fietsband harder soos jy meer lug daarin pomp?
options: More gas particles hit the walls of the tyre more often
The air turns into a liquid
optionsAf: Meer gasdeeltjies tref die wande van die band meer dikwels
questions.explain: Gas pressure comes from particles colliding with the walls. More particles mean more collisions and a higher pressure.
questions.explainAf: Gasdruk kom van deeltjies wat teen die wande bots. Meer deeltjies beteken meer botsings en 'n hoër druk.

questions.q: A glass rod is rubbed with silk and becomes positively charged. What happened to the glass?
questions.qAf: 'n Glasstaaf word met sy gevryf en word positief gelaai. Wat het met die glas gebeur?
options: It lost electrons to the silk
It gained electrons from the silk
It gained protons from the silk
optionsAf: Dit het elektrone aan die sy verloor
Dit het elektrone van die sy gekry
Dit het protone van die sy gekry
questions.explain: A material that loses electrons becomes positive. The silk gained those electrons and became negative.
questions.explainAf: 'n Stof wat elektrone verloor, word positief. Die sy het daardie elektrone gekry en het negatief geword.

questions.q: In a sound wave, what is a compression?
questions.qAf: Wat is 'n kompressie in 'n klankgolf?
options: A region where the particles are pushed close together
A region where the particles are spread far apart
The highest point of a transverse wave
A place where there are no particles
optionsAf: 'n Gebied waar die deeltjies naby aan mekaar gedruk word
'n Gebied waar die deeltjies ver uitmekaar versprei is
Die hoogste punt van 'n transversale golf
'n Plek waar daar geen deeltjies is nie
questions.explain: Compressions are high-pressure regions where particles bunch up; rarefactions are low-pressure regions where they spread out.
questions.explainAf: Kompressies is hoëdrukgebiede waar deeltjies saamdrom; verdunnings is laedrukgebiede waar hulle uitmekaar versprei.

questions.q: A learner plucks a guitar string harder without changing the note. What changes?
questions.qAf: 'n Leerder pluk 'n kitaarsnaar harder sonder om die noot te verander. Wat verander?
options: The amplitude, so the sound is louder
The frequency, so the pitch is higher
The speed of sound in the air
optionsAf: Die amplitude, dus is die klank harder
Die frekwensie, dus is die toonhoogte hoër
Die spoed van klank in die lug
questions.explain: A bigger vibration means a bigger amplitude and a louder sound. The pitch (frequency) stays the same, and so does the speed of sound in air.
questions.explainAf: 'n Groter vibrasie beteken 'n groter amplitude en 'n harder klank. Die toonhoogte (frekwensie) bly dieselfde, en so ook die spoed van klank in lug.

questions.q: About how far away must a hard surface be for you to hear a separate echo?
questions.qAf: Ongeveer hoe ver weg moet 'n harde oppervlak wees sodat jy 'n aparte weerklank hoor?
questions.explain: The echo must come back at least 0.1 s after the original sound has ended, which needs a surface about 17 m away.
questions.explainAf: Die weerklank moet minstens 0,1 s ná die oorspronklike klank terugkom, wat 'n oppervlak van ongeveer 17 m ver nodig het.

questions.q: Why can you not see a clear image of yourself in crumpled foil?
questions.qAf: Waarom kan jy nie 'n duidelike beeld van jouself in verfrommelde foelie sien nie?
options: The rough surface scatters the reflected light in many directions
optionsAf: Die growwe oppervlak versprei die weerkaatste lig in baie rigtings
Lig kan nie van metaal weerkaats nie
questions.explain: This is diffuse reflection. A smooth mirror reflects all the light in the same direction, so it gives a clear image.
questions.explainAf: Dit is diffuse weerkaatsing. 'n Gladde spieël weerkaats al die lig in dieselfde rigting, dus gee dit 'n duidelike beeld.

questions.q: Which of these materials is opaque?
questions.qAf: Watter een van hierdie materiale is ondeursigtig?
questions.explain: Light cannot pass through an opaque material such as brick, so it casts a shadow. Glass, clean water and clear plastic are transparent.
questions.explainAf: Lig kan nie deur 'n ondeursigtige materiaal soos baksteen gaan nie, dus werp dit 'n skaduwee. Glas, skoon water en helder plastiek is deursigtig.

questions.q: Sunlight takes about 8.3 minutes to reach Earth. What does this mean when you look at the Sun?
questions.qAf: Sonlig neem ongeveer 8,3 minute om die Aarde te bereik. Wat beteken dit wanneer jy na die Son kyk?
options: You see the Sun as it was about 8 minutes ago
You see the Sun as it will be in 8 minutes
The Sun is 8 light years away
Light from the Sun travels at 8 km/s
optionsAf: Jy sien die Son soos dit ongeveer 8 minute gelede was
Jy sien die Son soos dit oor 8 minute sal wees
Lig van die Son beweeg teen 8 km/s
questions.explain: Light takes time to travel, so you are looking into the past. Light from Alpha Centauri left it 4.3 years ago.
questions.explainAf: Lig neem tyd om te beweeg, dus kyk jy na die verlede. Lig van Alpha Centauri het dit 4,3 jaar gelede verlaat.

questions.q: Where is our solar system in the Milky Way?
questions.qAf: Waar is ons sonnestelsel in die Melkweg?
options: In one of the spiral arms, about 26 000 light years from the centre
optionsAf: In een van die spiraalarms, ongeveer 26 000 ligjaar van die middelpunt
questions.explain: We are in a spiral arm. When you see the Milky Way as a bright band across the sky, you are looking through the disc edge-on.
questions.explainAf: Ons is in 'n spiraalarm. Wanneer jy die Melkweg as 'n helder band oor die lug sien, kyk jy op sy kant deur die skyf.

questions.q: Which kind of telescope, such as the James Webb Space Telescope, can see through clouds of dust?
questions.qAf: Watter soort teleskoop, soos die James Webb-ruimteteleskoop, kan deur stofwolke sien?
questions.explain: Infrared telescopes detect infrared (heat) radiation, which passes through dust, so they can study very distant galaxies.
questions.explainAf: Infrarooiteleskope spoor infrarooi- (hitte-) straling op, wat deur stof gaan, dus kan hulle baie verafgeleë sterrestelsels bestudeer.

questions.q: What is special about SALT's primary mirror?
questions.qAf: Wat is spesiaal aan SALT se primêre spieël?
options: It is made of 91 smaller hexagonal mirrors
It is made of glass lenses only
optionsAf: Dit bestaan uit 91 kleiner seshoekige spieëls
questions.explain: SALT's primary mirror is about 11 m × 9.8 m, built from a hexagonal array of 91 smaller mirrors. MeerKAT is the 64-dish radio telescope.
questions.explainAf: SALT se primêre spieël is ongeveer 11 m × 9,8 m, gebou uit 'n seshoekige opstelling van 91 kleiner spieëls. MeerKAT is die radioteleskoop met 64 skottels.

questions.q: How did the solar system form?
questions.qAf: Hoe het die sonnestelsel gevorm?
options: From a giant rotating cloud of gas and dust, about 4.6 billion years ago
From a piece that broke off Jupiter
From a collision between two galaxies last century
optionsAf: Uit 'n reuse draaiende wolk van gas en stof, ongeveer 4,6 miljard jaar gelede
Uit 'n stuk wat van Jupiter afgebreek het
Uit 'n botsing tussen twee sterrestelsels in die vorige eeu
questions.explain: The solar system formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a rotating cloud of gas and dust. The Sun holds 99.86% of its mass.
questions.explainAf: Die sonnestelsel het ongeveer 4,6 miljard jaar gelede uit 'n draaiende wolk van gas en stof gevorm. Die Son bevat 99,86% van sy massa.

sections.title: True or false
sections.intro: Decide whether each statement is true or false.
sections.introAf: Besluit of elke stelling waar of onwaar is.

questions.q: Photosynthesis and cellular respiration are essentially reverse reactions of each other.
questions.qAf: Fotosintese en sellulêre respirasie is in wese omgekeerde reaksies van mekaar.
questions.explain: True. Photosynthesis takes in CO₂ and releases O₂; respiration takes in O₂ and releases CO₂. Together they cycle carbon.
questions.explainAf: Waar. Fotosintese neem CO₂ in en stel O₂ vry; respirasie neem O₂ in en stel CO₂ vry. Saam laat hulle koolstof sirkuleer.

questions.q: The alkali metals in Group 1 become more reactive further down the group.
questions.qAf: Die alkalimetale in Groep 1 word meer reaktief hoe verder af in die groep.
questions.explain: True. The outer electron is further from the nucleus and easier to remove.
questions.explainAf: Waar. Die buitenste elektron is verder van die kern af en makliker om te verwyder.

questions.q: Graphite is a non-metal that conducts electricity.
questions.qAf: Grafiet is 'n nie-metaal wat elektrisiteit gelei.
questions.explain: True. Graphite, a form of carbon, is a well-known exception to the rule that non-metals are poor conductors.
questions.explainAf: Waar. Grafiet, 'n vorm van koolstof, is 'n bekende uitsondering op die reël dat nie-metale swak geleiers is.

questions.q: Lightning is a huge discharge of static electricity.
questions.qAf: Weerlig is 'n reuse ontlading van statiese elektrisiteit.
questions.explain: True. Particles in a storm cloud rub together and the cloud becomes charged; when the charge is big enough, it discharges as lightning.
questions.explainAf: Waar. Deeltjies in 'n stormwolk vryf teen mekaar en die wolk word gelaai; wanneer die lading groot genoeg is, ontlaai dit as weerlig.

questions.q: Uranus and Neptune are ice giants.
questions.qAf: Uranus en Neptunus is ysreuse.
questions.explain: True. Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants; Uranus and Neptune are ice giants.
questions.explainAf: Waar. Jupiter en Saturnus is gasreuse; Uranus en Neptunus is ysreuse.

questions.q: There are only 12 officially recognised constellations.
questions.qAf: Daar is net 12 amptelik erkende sterrebeelde.
questions.explain: False. There are 88 officially recognised constellations.
questions.explainAf: Onwaar. Daar is 88 amptelik erkende sterrebeelde.

sections.title: Matching
sections.intro: Match column A to column B, and find the matching pairs.
sections.introAf: Pas kolom A by kolom B, en vind die pare wat bymekaar pas.

questions.q: Match each South African biome in column A with its description in column B.
questions.qAf: Pas elke Suid-Afrikaanse bioom in kolom A by sy beskrywing in kolom B.
pairs: Largest biome: grassland with scattered trees, Kruger
Knysna-Tsitsikamma, home of the Knysna loerie
pairsAf: Grootste bioom: grasveld met verspreide bome, Kruger
questions.explain: Fynbos is in the Western Cape, the savanna is the largest biome, the Succulent Karoo is a winter-rainfall desert, and the forest biome includes Knysna-Tsitsikamma.
questions.explainAf: Fynbos is in die Wes-Kaap, die savanne is die grootste bioom, die Sukkulente Karoo is 'n winterreënwoestyn, en die woudbioom sluit Knysna-Tsitsikamma in.

questions.q: Match each element in column A with a use in column B.
questions.qAf: Pas elke element in kolom A by 'n gebruik in kolom B.
questions.explain: Aluminium is light, malleable and resists corrosion; gold is lustrous and does not tarnish; chlorine kills harmful micro-organisms in water.
questions.explainAf: Aluminium is lig, smeebaar en weerstaan korrosie; goud is glansend en verkleur nie; chloor maak skadelike mikro-organismes in water dood.

questions.q: Find the matching pairs: link each circuit symbol to the component it stands for.
questions.qAf: Vind die pare wat bymekaar pas: koppel elke stroombaansimbool aan die komponent wat dit voorstel.
pairs: A circle with an A inside
A circle with an X inside
questions.explain: An ammeter is a circle with A, a resistor is a rectangle and a bulb is a circle with a cross inside. A voltmeter is a circle with V.
questions.explainAf: 'n Ampèremeter is 'n sirkel met A, 'n resistor is 'n reghoek en 'n gloeilamp is 'n sirkel met 'n kruis binne-in. 'n Voltmeter is 'n sirkel met V.

sections.title: Steps in order
sections.intro: Put the steps in the correct order.
sections.introAf: Plaas die stappe in die korrekte volgorde.

questions.q: Put these levels of scale in order from smallest to largest.
questions.qAf: Plaas hierdie skaalvlakke in volgorde van kleinste tot grootste.
questions.explain: Planet → planetary system → star cluster → galaxy → galaxy cluster → observable universe.
questions.explainAf: Planeet → planetêre stelsel → sterretros → sterrestelsel → sterrestelselgroep → waarneembare heelal.

sections.title: Scenarios
sections.intro: Read each scenario, then answer the questions about it.
sections.introAf: Lees elke scenario en beantwoord dan die vrae daaroor.

questions.scenario: A savanna grassland captures 50 000 kJ of energy through photosynthesis. Use the 10% rule.
questions.scenarioAf: 'n Savannegrasveld vang 50 000 kJ energie deur fotosintese vas. Gebruik die 10%-reël.

questions.q: How much energy is available to the primary consumers?
questions.qAf: Hoeveel energie is beskikbaar vir die primêre verbruikers?

questions.q: How much energy reaches the tertiary consumers (the top predators)?
questions.qAf: Hoeveel energie bereik die tersiêre verbruikers (die toproofdiere)?
questions.explain: 50 000 → 5 000 (primary) → 500 (secondary) → 50 kJ (tertiary).
questions.explainAf: 50 000 → 5 000 (primêr) → 500 (sekondêr) → 50 kJ (tersiêr).

questions.scenario: A learner tests three elements. Element X melts at 660 °C, conducts electricity and is shiny and silvery. Element Y melts at 115 °C, does not conduct and is dull and yellow. Element Z melts at 1 414 °C, conducts only partly and is shiny and grey.
questions.scenarioAf: 'n Leerder toets drie elemente. Element X smelt by 660 °C, gelei elektrisiteit en is blink en silwerkleurig. Element Y smelt by 115 °C, gelei nie en is dof en geel. Element Z smelt by 1 414 °C, gelei net gedeeltelik en is blink en grys.

questions.q: What is element X?
questions.qAf: Wat is element X?
questions.explain: It is shiny and conducts electricity: those are properties of a metal (it is aluminium).
questions.explainAf: Dit is blink en gelei elektrisiteit: dit is eienskappe van 'n metaal (dit is aluminium).

questions.q: What is element Y?
questions.qAf: Wat is element Y?
questions.explain: Dull, a poor conductor and a low melting point: a non-metal (it is sulfur).
questions.explainAf: Dof, 'n swak geleier en 'n lae smeltpunt: 'n nie-metaal (dit is swael).

questions.q: What is element Z?
questions.qAf: Wat is element Z?
questions.explain: Shiny like a metal but only partly conducting: a metalloid (it is silicon, a semiconductor used in computer chips).
questions.explainAf: Blink soos 'n metaal maar gelei net gedeeltelik: 'n metalloïed (dit is silikon, 'n halfgeleier wat in rekenaarskyfies gebruik word).

questions.scenario: To send 100 MW along a transmission line, about 9 090 A of current is needed at 11 kV, but only about 250 A at 400 kV. The heat lost in a cable increases sharply as the current increases.
questions.scenarioAf: Om 100 MW langs 'n transmissielyn te stuur, is ongeveer 9 090 A stroom by 11 kV nodig, maar net ongeveer 250 A by 400 kV. Die hitte wat in 'n kabel verlore gaan, neem skerp toe soos die stroom toeneem.

questions.q: About how many times bigger is the current at 11 kV than at 400 kV?
questions.qAf: Ongeveer hoeveel keer groter is die stroom by 11 kV as by 400 kV?

questions.q: Which transmission voltage wastes the least energy as heat?
questions.qAf: Watter transmissiespanning mors die minste energie as hitte?
questions.explain: At 400 kV the current is smallest, so the least energy is lost as heat in the cables.
questions.explainAf: By 400 kV is die stroom die kleinste, dus gaan die minste energie as hitte in die kabels verlore.

questions.q: A geyser blanket and a timer can cut a home's electricity use.
questions.qAf: 'n Geiserkombers en 'n tydskakelaar kan 'n huis se elektrisiteitsverbruik verminder.
questions.explain: True. Geysers are among the biggest users of electricity in a home.
questions.explainAf: Waar. Geisers is van die grootste gebruikers van elektrisiteit in 'n huis.
